title: Introduce conditional toolchain-watcher and devdep-curation to reduce presubmit flakiness
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Adds a conditional toolchain watcher, quarantines transient devdeps during presubmit, and reduces flakiness in SDK integration suites. Backwards-compatible; rollout gated behind flag.
commits: add: conditional toolchain watcher binary + integration shim
refactor: split devdeps into curated lists and quarantine runner
ci: add presubmit profile 'fast' with selective sdk-test gating
docs: doc stub for toolchain-watcher configuration and rollout plan
chore: bump test image and pin golang toolchain manifest
review_comments: Luis Ortega: Can the watcher be run as a short-lived job instead of a long-lived daemon? Concern about resource usage on small CI agents.
Ava Chen: Addressed — watcher now runs as a single run per presubmit with optional 'lease' mode for devbox sessions; updated main.go and docs.
Marta Nguyen: The devdep quarantine looks good, but we should ensure it doesn't hide real regressions in SDK tests. Suggest adding a telemetry tag for quarantined failures.
Ava Chen: Added telemetry tag 'devdep.quarantined=true' and exported a counter to Prometheus; included in rollout checklist.
Samir Patel: Please add an opt-out label for repos that still need full devdeps during presubmit (we need parity for some infra repos).
Ava Chen: Added PRESUBMIT_SKIP_QUARANTINE label handling and documented edge cases.
CI Bot: flaky sdk-tests/azure-integration failed on first run; rerun succeeded. Final CI status: all checks passed.
description:
Motivation: Presubmit runs have shown increasing nondeterministic failures in SDK integration suites (notably sdk/python/azure and sdk/ts/storage) caused by transient dev dependencies and occasional toolchain drift. This PR introduces a conservative, opt-in mechanism to (1) detect mismatched or stale toolchains used by CI agents (toolchain-watcher), (2) quarantine and re-run tests that fail due to transient devdeps to reduce noisy flakes (devdep-curation), and (3) expose a lightweight presubmit profile for fast feedback on PRs that touch only docs or small infra changes.

Goals: Reduce developer pain from noisy presubmit failures, speed up typical PR feedback loops, and keep release automation informed about dependency-refresh events so downstream release hooks can annotate or pause rollouts. Important constraints: changes must be non-breaking for repos that opt out, and rollout should be reversible and observable.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a new small binary infra/toolchain-watcher integrated into the presubmit pipeline. The watcher compares the agent runtime (go/node/python versions, pinned toolchain manifest) against a manifest stored in ci/images/toolchain-manifest.json and fails fast with a structured message if mismatch is detected. In 'lease' mode it can pin a short-lived devimage lease to speed up subsequent runs.
- Adds tools/devdep-curator which implements a quarantine flow: if a test fails with signatures matching configured transient patterns (network/timeouts/403 rate limits from registries), the job records the failure with a telemetry tag and reruns the test in a clean curated devdeps environment. If rerun passes, failure is marked quarantine and surfaced to a 'quarantine' dashboard for triage rather than blocking merges.
- Introduces ci/presubmit-profiles.yaml with a new 'fast' profile used for PRs that change only markdown, docs, or targeted config files; 'fast' runs linters and smoke tests only. Full matrix runs remain the default for code changes.
- Adds minimal release automation hook: release/automation/annotate-dep-refresh.go will add a release note annotation when a presubmit run triggers an automated devdep update (Linear integration stub is included).
- Adds documentation and rollout plan under docs/ci/toolchain-watcher.md and an internal checklist in the PR description.

Checklist (release gating):
- [x] toolchain-watcher binary + tests
- [x] devdep-curator proof-of-concept + telemetry counters
- [x] presubmit profile and workflow updates with opt-out label support (PRESUBMIT_SKIP_QUARANTINE)
- [x] docs and runbook for oncall
- [x] release hook stub to annotate dep-refresh events
- [x] canary rollout to 10% of presubmits (implemented via workflow input, currently enabled for handful of SDK repos)

Why this is safe: Default behaviour is unchanged unless a repo opts into curated devdep handling or uses the 'fast' profile. Quarantine does not auto-suppress legitimate regressions; quarantined failures are recorded and surfaced for triage. Toolchain-watcher fails fast with an explanatory message and a link to the manifest diff; it can be disabled via CI input for legacy agents.

Testing and CI notes: Initial CI run showed a flaky failure in sdk/python/azure integration test on the first run (network timeout to test fixture). The devdep-curator detected the pattern and reran in a curated environment; rerun passed. After a follow-up tweak to retry thresholds the CI pipeline passed all checks. Unit tests included for watcher manifest parsing and quarantine signature matching.

Rollout plan and observability:
- Day 0: Merge with flag disabled globally; enable for sdk/python and sdk/typescript presubmits (10% canary).
- Day 1-3: Monitor 'ci.quarantine_count' and 'ci.toolchain_mismatch' metrics; review quarantine dashboard weekly.
- Day 7: If stable, broaden to all SDK repos.
- Opt-out policy: Repos can set PRESUBMIT_SKIP_QUARANTINE label or set presubmit-profiles.yaml entry to 'legacy'.

Related: ENG-2345 (reduce presubmit flakiness), ENG-2350 (release automation annotations), SUP-987 (customer-facing incident that motivated quicker rollback diagnostics).

High-level commits and changes: commit list included above. Key changed files: ci/presubmit-profiles.yaml (adds 'fast' profile), infra/toolchain-watcher (new component), tools/devdep-curator (quarantine logic and runner shim), .github/workflows/presubmit.yml (conditional steps for new profile), docs/ci/toolchain-watcher.md (runbook), release/automation/annotate-dep-refresh.go (release annotation stub).

Notes for reviewers: Focus on the quarantine signature whitelist (tools/devdep-curator/README) and the opt-out label semantics. The watcher implementation is intentionally conservative — it surfaces mismatches rather than auto-rolling images. We will follow up with a smaller PR to add a self-healing mode if the team wants it.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main after approvals from Luis, Marta, and Samir. CI green on final run.

If something goes wrong: Revert the merge or set global flag to disable devdep-curation (CI input: DEVDEP_CURATION=off). Runbook includes steps to remove leases and clear quarantine state.
